top_cited_works.title: Steady Aerodynamic Theory for Porous Membrane Wings
top_cited_works.abstract: The growing interest in small-scale uncrewed air vehicles (UAVs) for surveillance, reconnaissance, and urban mobility purposes continues to spur scientific interest in novel aerodynamic design solutions inspired by biological fliers. A special focus has been given to compliant membrane wings, which passively adapt their shape to accommodate the flow. The coupled fluid-structure interaction inherent to these flexible structures has been shown to improve aerodynamic performance in steady flow by delaying the onset of stall and enhancing lift. However, these benefits were identified for impermeable membranes, whereas in nature similar compliant structures commonly include porosity. Such permeability enables flow seepage through the airfoil surface, which alters the pressure distribution and reduces the aerodynamic load on the airfoil in steady flow conditions. For a flexible membrane wing, such flow seepage also alters the membrane camber line through its tight coupling with the surrounding flow. top_cited_works.title: On membrane-wing stability in laminar flow
Unsteady aerodynamic theory for membrane wings
top_cited_works.abstract: We study analytically the dynamic response of membrane aerofoils subject to arbitrary, small-amplitude chord motions and transverse gusts in a two-dimensional inviscid incompressible flow. The theoretical model assumes linear deformations of an extensible membrane under constant tension, which are coupled aeroelastically to external aerodynamic loads using unsteady thin aerofoil theory. The structural and aerodynamic membrane responses are investigated for harmonic heave oscillations, an instantaneous change in angle of attack, sinusoidal transverse gusts and a sharp-edged gust. The unsteady lift responses for these scenarios produce aeroelastic extensions to the Theodorsen, Wagner, Sears and Küssner functions, respectively, for a membrane aerofoil. These extensions incorporate for the first time membrane fluid–structure interaction into the expressions for the unsteady lift response of a flexible aerofoil. recent_works.title: Unsteady aerodynamic theory and experiments of hovering membrane wings
recent_works.abstract: We investigate the unsteady lift response of compliant membrane wings in hovering kinematics by combining analytical inviscid theory with experimental results. An unsteady aerodynamic model is derived for a compliant thin aerofoil immersed in incompressible inviscid flow of variable free-stream velocity at high angles of attack. The model, representing a spanwise section of a hovering membrane wing, assumes small membrane deformation and attached flow. These assumptions are supported by experiments showing that passive membrane deformation suppresses flow separation when hovering at angles of attack up to $55^\circ$ . An analytically derived expression is obtained for the unsteady lift response, incorporating the classical Wagner and Theodorsen functions and the membrane dynamic response. This theoretical expression is validated against experimental water-tank measurements that are performed on hovering membrane wings at angles of attack of $35^\circ$ and $55^\circ$ . Data from membrane deformation measurements is applied to the theoretical lift expression, providing the theoretical lift response prediction for each of the available experimental scenarios.
